name: Basilica of the National Shrine of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
history: The first Catholic cathedral built in the United States after independence, raised under John Carroll, the first American bishop. Latrobe offered a Gothic and a Neoclassical design; Carroll chose the Neoclassical as a statement that American Catholicism belonged to the new republic. It opened on 31 May 1821. Most of the first American bishops were consecrated here, and the Third Plenary Council here commissioned the Baltimore Catechism.
arch: Considered the masterpiece of Benjamin Henry Latrobe, the "Father of American Architecture" and Jefferson's Architect of the Capitol: a Greek portico of Ionic columns, two cylindrical towers with onion domes, and a great dome.
features: Thomas Jefferson suggested the wooden outer dome with 24 half-visible skylights.
A 32-month, $34 million restoration finished in the 21st century returned the original light-filled design.

look.d: Jefferson suggested the double-shell dome with 24 skylights.
A temple front chosen to say: Catholic and American.
Once doubted as Latrobe's, the onion domes are now believed to be his own design.

fun: It is often called "America's First Cathedral".
journal: Latrobe, Carroll and Jefferson's skylights. The light falls like the Enlightenment itself.
